19199: When animals are treated with a combination of suboptimal doses of Molnupiravir and Favipiravir (that each alone result in respectively a 1.3 log10 and 1.1 log10 reduction of infectious virus titers in the lungs), a marked combined potency is observed. Infectious virus titers in the lungs of animals treated with the combo are on average reduced by 4.5 log10 and infectious virus are no longer detected in the lungs of 60% of treated infected animals.

In the combo-treated hamsters an increased frequency of C-to-T and G-to-A mutations in the viral RNA is observed as compared to the single treatment groups which may explain the pronounced antiviral potency of the combination.

We first demonstrate that Molnupiravir can reduce infectious virus titers in lungs of infected animals in a dose-dependent manner by up to 3.5 log10 which is associated with a marked improvement of virus-induced lung pathology.

When start of treatment was delayed with one day a reduction of titers in the lungs of 2.4 log10 was achieved. Moreover, treatment of infected animals nearly completely prevented transmission to co-housed untreated sentinels.

Primary label is minor: the core assertion of marked combined potency with suboptimal doses is preserved, but the magnitude shifts from '4.5 log10' to '∼5 log10' (relative change ~10%, below 20% threshold) and '60%' to '>60%', with wording changes that do not alter direction, scope, or effect-type class, and hedging remains unchanged (both use 'is observed'). S1 label is minor: the published version drops 'G-to-A mutations' from the list of observed mutation types, which is a scope narrowing within the same mechanistic claim, but the core mechanistic explanation remains intact with the same hedging ('may explain'). S2 label is major: the preprint's second secondary claim about Molnupiravir's dose-dependent monotherapy effect (3.5 log10 reduction, lung pathology improvement) is replaced in the published version by new findings on delayed treatment efficacy and transmission prevention, constituting a claim replacement.
